summary: Chippewa County, MI tower near Raco, built about 1923-1925 for the Forest Service; CCC crews were to man it in 1940; NHLR-registered 2022 as US 1576; no access information found.

facts.status_note: Latest evidence is a 2021 photograph on the NHLR page; we found no later check of its condition.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Hiawatha National Forest (NHLR)

staffing.status: CCC enrollees from the Raco camp announced to man the tower

events.note: A June 21, 1923 newspaper item says the ranger station and tower were being completed. NHLR gives 'circa 1925' as the build date.
A May 1, 1940 newspaper item says CCC enrollees from the Raco camp would man the tower.
Added to the register May 22, 2022 as US 1576, MI 7.

evidence.supports: tower sits atop the highest hill near Raco, Michigan
evidence.quote: Built about 1925, Demond Hill Fire Tower sits atop the highest hill near the lumbering town of Raco, Michigan.

evidence.supports: location in Chippewa County, Michigan, Hiawatha National Forest
administered by the U.S. Forest Service
June 1923 newspaper: station and tower being completed at Demond Hill
evidence.quote: A new forest ranger station and fire lookout tower, located at Demond Hill west of Raco, is being completed by the ranger for this district.

evidence.supports: worked with the Raco CCC camp to handle fire suppression during the Depression (NHLR)
evidence.quote: During the Great Depression, the tower worked in conjunction with the Civilian Conservation Corps camp in Raco to handle fire suppression.

evidence.supports: May 1940 newspaper: CCC enrollees from Raco camp to man the tower
evidence.quote: The Demond Hill fire tower will be manned by CCC enrollees from Raco CCC Camp.

evidence.supports: by 1942 Raco was the only camp left; protection area 151,140 acres
evidence.quote: By 1942, when Raco was the only camp left in the district, its fire protection area covered 151,140 acres.

evidence.supports: added to the register on May 22, 2022

corrections.why: A June 21, 1923 newspaper item, quoted on Forest Lookouts, says the ranger station and tower were being completed. NHLR's circa 1925 is an estimate. The story gives both; the editor should confirm which date to show.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says circa 1925; a June 1923 newspaper says the tower was being completed. We record 1923 as the earliest documented date and keep NHLR's circa 1925 in the event note.

notes_for_editor: No design, height or access source was found, so those keys are omitted. The NHLR page shows a 2021 photo, but no later check. A geocaching listing describes current radio use, but its page did not load in our fetch, so the story makes no claim about that. Two Facebook posts from the Forest Fire Lookout Association and two NARA photographs appeared in search results only and were not used.
